status: PROVED (large-box averaging; no periodicity of phi required)
statement: a bounded transfer (|phi| <= Phi, divergence >= b) on a packing of finite upper density that is D-saturated for some finite D implies rho <= 1/sqrt(32)
hypotheses: D-saturation: every point of space within D of a centre (equivalent to diam Omega(v) <= D; LEMMA S)
lemma_B: D-saturation gives |U*| = |B| + O_D(L^2): cells of centres in B lie in B grown by D, and every point of B at distance > D from the boundary lies in a cell of a centre in B
why_saturation_is_needed: sum_{v in Lambda cap B} vol Omega(v) = |B| + O(L^2) does NOT follow from the cells tiling space: FCC in a half-space has empty intersection with a box in the void, so the sum is 0 while |B| = L^3
corollary_1: K15-C-CUTIMPLIES-003: the finite-U cut condition alone, at any finite Phi, forces rho <= 1/sqrt(32) (take U = Lambda cap B)
corollary_2: a D-saturated packing with rho > 1/sqrt(32) admits no bounded transfer and violates some finite cut
does_not_apply_to: packings that are not D-saturated, e.g. the period-16 13-cluster (cells of diameter >= 12.3); there the cut/flow work is a refutation of a capacity, not a density bound
method: sum the divergence bound over a box of side L; antisymmetry cancels interior edges; crossing edges are O(rho R L^2) and the volume is L^3, so the mean of b tends to 0 and sqrt32 rho - 1 <= 0
supersedes: the earlier periodic-sum argument, which needed phi periodic -- a hypothesis the conclusion does not supply
withdrawn: the inference that this implication makes the transfer route 'circular'; a sufficient condition implying Kepler is not circular unless its proof assumes Kepler
